feat(apply): --private-new saves every object a run creates as private (#155)

Some trees show guests only what the owner chose to make public, but gwt-apply created every new object public, so each run had to be hidden by hand.
`gwt-apply --private-new` sets private on every object the run creates (person, family, event, place, source, citation, media, note), at the one place all creates pass through. Tags have no private flag in Gramps and are left alone.
Objects that already exist keep their value, a rerun of a landed list makes nothing private, and the docs say who still sees private objects (members and above) and how gwt-check and gwt-leads treat them. Off by default.
A command-line test and two mutant rows guard the flag and its wiring.

+    assert not fake.store["people"]["anna"].get("private")  # changed, not created: keeps its own value"},{"sha":"9e2026093f1ce3261610c97758df6ca34a2b85bb","filename":"docs/apply.md","status":"modified","additions":9,"deletions":1,"changes":10,"blob_url":"https://github.com/GeiserX/gramps-web-toolkit/blob/a8f5b83915354bbc0b6c7917c9f3dae284c5bc79/docs%2Fapply.md","raw_url":"https://github.com/GeiserX/gramps-web-toolkit/raw/a8f5b83915354bbc0b6c7917c9f3dae284c5bc79/docs%2Fapply.md","contents_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/GeiserX/gramps-web-toolkit/contents/docs%2Fapply.md?ref=a8f5b83915354bbc0b6c7917c9f3dae284c5bc79","patch":"@@ -25,7 +25,7 @@ On a multi-tree server, the tree comes from the user: the login (`POST /api/toke

+Other flags: `--verify` and `--json FILE` ([Prove a list landed](#prove-a-list-landed)), `--log PATH`, `--retries N` (default 5, at least 1), `--retry-wait SECONDS` (default 30), `--snapshot FILE`, `--save-snapshot FILE` and `--since OLD` ([Snapshots](#snapshots)), `--tag NAME` ([Tags](#tags)), `--private-new` ([Private by default](#private-by-default)), `--break-lock` (below).
 
 Every run gets a run id, `<date>-<time>-<6 hex>`. The first line of output names it and the log, before the login, so a run whose login fails still says which run it was. The log path carries `(created once logged in)`: the file appears only after the login. See [The log](#the-log).
 
@@ -210,6 +210,14 @@ The merge itself is the server's (`POST /api/people/<winner>/merge/<loser>`, `PO
 
 Before the merge, the winner gets a note that records it: `Merged Person I0042 (John Smith) into this person (ruling R-12). <reason>`. The note is how a rerun knows the merge is done: when the loser is gone and the winner has that note, the op is skipped; when the loser is gone and there is no note, the op is a conflict.
 
+### Private by default
+
+`--private-new` saves every object the run creates with `private` set: a person, family, event, place, source, citation, media object or note. The tags `--tag` makes are not marked, because a Gramps tag has no private flag. Gramps Web hides private objects from a guest login, so a tree that shows guests only a chosen set of people never shows a new object to them. Members and every role above them still see private objects. Without the flag every created object is public; no op can set `private`.
+
+The flag covers only the objects this run creates. An object that already exists keeps its own value: the objects the run changes, and the ones an earlier run made without the flag. A rerun of a list that already landed skips every op, so it makes nothing private, and `--verify` does not compare `private`. Mark those by hand in Gramps Web.
+
+Private objects are also hidden from some of the toolkit's own reading. `gwt-check` reports each new object under its `private` check (leave that out with `--ignore-check private`, [check options](check.md#options-of-check)), and it does not read private citations and notes as evidence for a parent link ([links](check.md#what-the-records-say-about-parent-links-links)) or for an act. `gwt-leads` holds back private people and ignores private events.
+
 ## Prove a list landed
 
 `--verify` answers "is this list in the tree?". It is a dry run: it writes nothing and takes no lock. It exits `0` when every op comes out `skip`, and `1` when any op would write, conflicts or errs. Under each op that would write, it says why:"}]}
